build: version 1.0, eight D64 images (archive.org d64_Pool_of_Radiance_v1.0_1988_SSI_Disk_1_of_4_Side_A); BOOT prints "POOL OF RADIANCE, VERSION 1.0"

comments.text: This file's cancel: the effect in hand ($2AFC) none, the damage 0 and IS UNAFFECTED (message $0C). SPELLE01 has its own at the same address; combat-set's $9927 calls whichever is loaded.
A timed effect for each combatant the mummy's fear reaches: A the save byte, X the time's base, Y the kind; no time per level; then target_effect with a fourth byte of 0, and find_entry for the kind.
The effect's fourth byte = A, the target loaded, slot 7's file kept for later, its saving throw (save_roll) and the effect (spell_effect, which needs the save to fail), the file not reloaded.

Kind 82, the mummy's (event 8, the battle's start). The mummy's side kept ($A4E2) and IS PARALYZED (message 7) as the message. Every combatant in the fight on the other side: a d4 for the time in rounds, then the save byte from zero-page $21, $40 more for a human (race 7), and kind $34 (52, held, kind_helpless's lose a turn) through effect_kind_y. Then kind 82 is taken off the mummy, so it happens once a battle. The spell record's range ($2B32) is not cleared first, as charm_gaze clears it.

LDA $21 reads zero page, not the number $21 (LDA #$21): no code in the listing writes $21, and it holds 0 in every snapshot. So a non-human's save byte is 0, which allows no save (save_roll), and a human's is $40, a save of type 0 with 2 added to the roll. With #$21 every target would save with 1 added, and a human with 3.

Kind 84 (event 14, its turn), a charming gaze no monster file gives: GAZES... (message $14), then CHARM PERSON's effect (kind $0B) with message 0, IS CHARMED, on the target: a spell record of zeros (no hit roll), save byte $D1 (save 4, the spell save, needed 2 higher), and a fourth byte of the gazer's side ($A4E2) with bits 1 and 2 set.

Kind 85 (events 2 and 3, after a hit), the wight's and wraith's: IS DRAINED (message $0B) for the target. Its full hit points divided by its levels in all four class parts ($6BC9-$6BCC) are lost (drain_hp). Then drained_part picks the class part, which loses a level ($6BA1 counts the levels lost); one at level 0 leaves the character GONE ($82). One with no hit points left is DEAD ($83). Then the character is worked out again for its new levels: rebuild.
One hit point each time from the full ($6B76), the base roll ($6BED, not below 0) and the hit points now ($6C19), counted in $6BA2, until X runs out or the hit points now reach 0.

The class part with the most experience behind its level loses one (top_part, a_A92C). For a character whose parts are all at level 1 every part needs 0 experience and none is picked, so a_A92C keeps what it held: 0, the magic-user's, when the file has just loaded, or the part of the last character drained. When that part is one the character does not have, its level goes from 0 to 255 and the character is not left GONE: the hit points are gone, so it is DEAD, which the temple's RAISE DEAD accepts.
With hit points left the character stays; with none it is DEAD ($83, set_drained).

The character's figures from its new levels, from this file's own tables rather than training's (gen's): the level shown ($6BA0) the drained part's; the experience points ($6BE8-$6BEA) the least the drained part's new level needs; the turning figure ($6BA4) the cleric level, one more from level 4 (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, as training's cleric_figures); the spell counts ($6BEE-$6BF0, cleric's in the high four bits, magic-user's in the low) from the tables below, with wisdom's extra cleric spells (wis_extra); the to-hit figure ($6B71) the best of the four parts' tables; the fighter level into $6B98; then compute_combat_stats and the character stored.
Six NOPs: code taken out of the turning figure's working.

Wisdom less 13 counts the extra cleric spells: two chances for the first level, two for the second, one for the third, each taken only while the count lasts and a level has spells. So 14 gives one first-level spell more, 15 two, 16 a second-level one, 17 two, 18 a third-level one; training gives two first-level spells from 13, one second-level at 15 and two at 16, and a third-level one from 17.
The magic-user's counts have no extra spells.
The to-hit figure: the best of the class parts' (keep_best).
Condition X ($82 GONE or $83 DEAD) for the character, which is stored (store_both); one that was still in the fight is reported IS KILLED (the combat's $0DC2) and taken off the screen (sprites_off).
A wisdom chance: the count (area_entry) less one; while it is not below 0, a spell level with any spells (A) gets one more.
The to-hit figure ($6B71) becomes A when A is higher.

Of the class parts the character has (level not 0), the one whose present level needed the most experience: the figure into best_xp, the part into a_A92C. A tie keeps the first found, from the fighter's (3) down; no part beats 0 when all are at level 1.
The most experience a class part's level needed, 24 bits ($A926-$A928), from top_part.
best_xp's middle byte.
best_xp's high byte.
The class part's figure being compared, 24 bits, low byte first ($A929-$A92B).
The class part energy_drain takes a level from: 0 magic-user, 1 cleric, 2 thief, 3 fighter. 0 in the file on disk.

Experience at the start of each level, levels 1 to 9, twelve bytes a level: three for each class part in the order magic-user, cleric, thief, fighter, high byte first. Level 2: 2,501, 1,501, 1,251 and 2,001. $FFFFFF for a level the part cannot reach (the magic-user and cleric past 6, the fighter past 8). The same figures as the 1st edition's tables.
Cleric first-level spells by cleric level 0-6: 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3.
Cleric second-level spells by cleric level 0-6: 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3. Training's cleric_slots gives one fewer at levels 2, 3 and 4 (0, 1, 2).
Cleric third-level spells by cleric level 0-6: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2.
The cleric's to-hit figure (60 less the THAC0) by level 0-6: 0, 40, 40, 40, 42, 42, 42, as training's.
Magic-user first-level spells by level 0-6: 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4, as training's mu_slots.
Magic-user second-level spells by level 0-6: 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2.
Magic-user third-level spells by level 0-6: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2.
The magic-user's to-hit figure by level 0-6: 0, 40, 40, 40, 40, 40, 41. Training's to_hit_table has 39 for levels 1 to 5, so a drained magic-user hits a little better.
The thief's to-hit figure by level 0-9: 0, 40, 40, 40, 40, 41, 41, 41, 41, 44. Training's has 39 for levels 1 to 4.
The fighter's to-hit figure by level 0-8: 40, 40, 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, as training's.
Kind 86 (events 2 and 3), the spectre's and vampire's: energy_drain, the entry stored, and a second drain unless the first left the character GONE ($82).

Kind 87 (events 2 and 3), the mummy's: timed effects $32 (50) for 10 days and $39 (57) for 30 days on the target (add_effect), its condition byte $21 (OK, with bit 5, which nothing in the listing reads), $6C1F a d6, and IS DISEASED (message 4).
Kind 91 (event 6, a spell's damage), the juju zombie's: MAGIC MISSILE (spell 15) is cancelled with IS UNAFFECTED; electricity (dmg_kind bit 2) does no damage.
Not MAGIC MISSILE: electricity does none.

Kind 94 (event 5), the juju zombie's: a weapon whose type's byte 7 ($6D93) is $80 (blunt: club, mace, flail, hammer, staff, sling ...) or 1 (piercing: dagger, spear, pike, arrows, quarrels ...) does half damage.
Kind 103 (event 13, going down), the vampire's: TURNS INTO GAS (message $17), and the combat's $1719 gives every square of it condition $86, fled.
Kind 115 (event 5), the skeletons': a weapon whose type's byte 7 is 0 or has bit 0 set does half damage; a blunt one ($80) does full.
Kind 116 (event 5), the mummy's: a weapon with a magical plus ($6D80) does half damage.
Half the damage unless Z is set.
The damage ($A4F7) halved.
Kind 117 (event 5), every undead's: a weapon of type $55, a vial of holy water, does 2 to 7 (roll_die 6, plus 1).
The damage = X.
Kind 119 (event 5): no damage from an attack without a weapon or from a weapon without a magical plus.
No damage from a weapon without a magical plus.
The damage 0.

Kinds 96 and 123 (event 5), the wight's and the wraith's: no damage without a weapon. A weapon whose third word ($6D7F) is SILVER (177) hits: for the wight (the kind in hand, $6E6E, is 96) in full, for the wraith at half. Any other needs a magical plus (needs_plus).
Kind 122 (events 5 and 6), the mummy's: a weapon of type $56, a flask of oil, does 3d8; magical fire (dmg_kind exactly 9) does one more a die ($2B0E, the dice rolled).

Kind 126 (event 1, when picked as a target), the vampire's: when the target has a readied item ($6D82 bit 7) with word $76 (118, MIRROR) among its three, or word $98 (HOLY SYMBOL) with WOODEN ($FC) as its third word, it cannot be picked ($2B17 = $FF). The game's mirrors are SILVER MIRROR and BRASS MIRROR; of its holy symbols only the WOODEN HOLY SYMBOL OF TYR and the WOODEN HOLY SYMBOL count, not the SILVER one of Sune, the IRON one of Tempus, the LEATHER one or the WOOD one.
